summary: T1-03 round 2. All three story checks pass. The two round-1 Codex blockers (windowed range read, unreadable ROI shapefile) are fixed and have tests. The two round-1 Claude low findings were fairly rebutted. I did not run fetch because it needs the network. I did not read pilot.py line by line, and I did not re-check the range-read window decoding in detail. Those parts rest on the passing tests.

checks.evidence: 981 passed, 2 xfailed. The xfails are the T1-01 schema-case fixtures, which are outside this story.

checks.criterion: Check: uv run python -m terraluna_pipeline.pilot check pgda78
checks.command: uv run python -m terraluna_pipeline.pilot check pgda78

checks.evidence: ruff check passed, ruff format --check passed (16 files) and mypy reported no issues in 16 source files.

checks.criterion: AC1: CLI fetch/record/check; record and check offline and deterministic; tests
checks.evidence: test_pilot.py:44-57 refuses sockets in an autouse fixture. test_pilot.py:1175 is test_record_and_check_run_offline. check against the real data/raw passes. I did not separately inspect the test that proves check leaves files unchanged.

checks.evidence: The diff adds io.read_remote_geotiff_window and test_io_remote_window.py (450 lines), and test_pilot.py has tests for the range-read fallback. I did not run fetch.

checks.evidence: outputs/pilot/pgda78_site01.json (746 lines) and the preview PNG (80,833 bytes) are tracked. check passes against the real data. The unreadable-ROI fix has tests. I did not read the JSON field by field.

checks.criterion: AC4: sources.json upserted and sorted, fetch fails non-zero on unreachable URL
checks.evidence: outputs/sources.json is tracked (128 lines added) and is validated by check. I did not run fetch against a failing URL.

checks.criterion: AC5: only small files committed; data/raw ignored
checks.evidence: Tracked files are only the pilot JSON, the 80,833-byte preview PNG and sources.json. Nothing under data/ is tracked.

findings.claim: The committed real-data record depends on a local data/raw that was not independently re-fetched in this review.
findings.evidence: check passes against local data/raw. It cross-checks sha256 and size against fetch.json, but I did not run fetch, which needs the network.

resolution.reason: Not a defect in the change: it states a limit of the review scope (the reviewer did not run fetch, which needs the network), and it repeats claude-r1-2, which was rebutted for the same reason. By the story design, fetch is the only network command and the gate runs only the offline check. check stays tied to the fetched bytes: _load_fetch in pilot.py (lines 257-289) refuses any raw file whose size or sha256 differs from data/raw/pgda78/fetch.json, and check pgda78 passes. For independent evidence, on 2026-11-14 from 20:15:41Z to 20:22:00Z the author downloaded every Site01 file again with curl from its recorded URL into a fresh temporary directory outside the repository; data/raw was not touched. All six returned HTTP 200 with byte counts and sha256 equal to fetch.json and to the checksums in outputs/sources.json: surf 3ba7b97c... (40980810 B), ldec 16d6ed21... (40980744 B), slp 3a90035a... (40980776 B), toterr cf2cf52f... (40980810 B), slperr 52bc3b23... (40980810 B), Site01_ROIs.tgz 40b96141... (2934 B). The committed record therefore describes the files the provider serves now. No code change is needed.
